title: Changing the page
summary: Create elements with JavaScript, style them with classList and attributes, and add them to the page.

quiz.q: Put these steps in the right order to add a new list item to the page.
quiz.explain: Find the parent, create the element, fill it, and only then attach it. An element that is never appended stays invisible.

quiz.q: Which line adds the CSS class `done` to an element named `item`?
quiz.explain: `classList` has `add`, `remove`, `toggle` and `contains`. It adds one class without disturbing the others.

quiz.q: Complete the line so the link points to the course website.
quiz.explain: `setAttribute(name, value)` sets any HTML attribute. Use `getAttribute(name)` to read it back.
The class `card` was added and then removed, so `contains('card')` is `false`.

exercise.task:
The page has an empty `<ul id="list">`. The starter already has an array `names`.

In `change.js`, for each name:

- create an `li` and set its text to the name,
- add the class `student`,
- set the attribute `data-name` to the name,
- append it to `#list`.

Then add the extra class `first` to the first `li` only.
hints: Use a loop over `names`. Inside it, create the element with `document.createElement('li')`.

`item.classList.add('student')` adds a class and `item.setAttribute('data-name', name)` adds the attribute. `list.append(item)` puts it on the page. After the loop, select the first `.student` and add `first`.
